# Daybook for judges

Ten minutes, four criteria. Each section starts with the fastest way to check it yourself. Chain numbers are as of 19 Nov 2026, 15:49:19 UTC (Lasna block 8,744,670); `make verify` rebuilds all of them from public RPCs.

Daybook runs on testnets only (Reactive Lasna, Base Sepolia, Unichain Sepolia). I have no mainnet funds for it right now.

- Each payment was delivered exactly once (0 duplicate deliveries).

Check it: open any link above, or run `make verify`, which re-derives every field of every CSV row from receipts and logs and compares it (13 rows).

## Integration

- Dynamic subscriptions: each invoice subscribes to `Transfer` into its pay address on creation and unsubscribes with the same arguments on settlement ([ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)).
- Callbacks to two chains from one reaction: v1-L5-crosschain paid half on Base and half on Unichain; the covering reaction sent one settlement to each chain and each was acknowledged on its own.
- Cron only while timed work is open, resend on a missing ack, and receipts through EAS on each payment chain.

## Usefulness

Trigger your own loop without a wallet:

1. Open https://daybook-omni.vercel.app and press **Pay a demo invoice**. A demo wallet sends 0.10 test USDC on Base Sepolia to a real open demo invoice.
2. Follow **Open its pay page**. It shows the payment seen, then stamps Paid with the receipt and the three linked transactions once the till's settlement is acknowledged.
3. Open https://daybook-omni.vercel.app/ledger for every inflow, matched or flagged, with a CSV export, and https://daybook-omni.vercel.app/health for how long it has run and what it cost.

Health from chain at the snapshot: running since 19 Nov 2026, 6 of 11 invoices settled, 5 open, 0.5144 lREACT spent on 16 measured reactions.

The ledger, rebuilt from chain: 10 transfers into v1 pay addresses on both payment chains: 8 matched to an invoice, 1 flagged as a wrong token, 1 in a token the invoice does not accept and does not watch, so it was never delivered, 0 unaccounted for. 7 of 7 acknowledged settlements had their tax, team and treasury shares recomputed from the policy and matched to the callback's transfers, and no accepted token was left at a settled pay address.

## Limits

- **Testnet only.** Everything runs on Reactive Lasna, Base Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia with test USDC. I have no mainnet funds for Daybook right now, so there is no mainnet deployment, no real money in it and no mainnet history to show.
- **Amounts are public.** Invoice amounts, pay addresses, payers and the split are on chain for anyone to read. Only client names and notes stay off chain, and the chain holds just their hash.
- **Trust in Reactive.** Settlement depends on Reactive Network delivering the payment log and relaying the callback. If it stops, money waits safely at the pay address and the owner can sweep it by hand (`DaybookTill.sweep`), but nothing settles on its own.
- **Unaudited, so capped.** The contracts had an internal adversarial review (docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md) and no external audit. Read from chain at the snapshot, the till caps are 20.00 USDC per settlement on Unichain Sepolia and 20.00 USDC per settlement on Base Sepolia, and the reactive contract refuses any invoice above 20.00 USDC.
- **The REACT balance runs out.** Every reaction is paid from the reactive contract's lREACT. When it hits zero the contract goes into debt and the network stops calling it until someone tops it up; the Health page shows the balance and how many reactions it still pays for.

Everything else is in [docs/LIMITS.md](docs/LIMITS.md).
